Generated with Codex CLI image_generation (sheet strokes, mark 1), ink extracted to alpha by assets/scripts/extract.mjs. Prompt:
STYLE — applies to everything in this image:
- It must look like a real flatbed scan of an actual hand-made drawing on plain white paper, made by Norma, a 70-year-old retired Argentine art teacher ("profesora de plástica") who now makes ceramics. Her hand is experienced and confident, but she works fast and doesn't fuss: lines are loose and a little imperfect.
- Medium: black India ink applied with a worn round watercolor brush. Visible pressure variation along each stroke (thick to thin), dry-brush breakup where the brush ran out of ink, slightly ragged edges, a few tiny ink specks, stroke ends that taper or end in a small blob, shapes that don't perfectly close.
- Pure black ink only. No grey wash, no colour, no shading, no hatching.
- Background: perfectly flat pure white (#FFFFFF). No paper texture, no shadows, no vignette, no scanner edges, no border, nothing else on the page, so the ink can be extracted cleanly.
- Avoid anything that looks digital: no vector-perfect curves, no symmetry, no font-like lettering, no glossy, 3D or neon effects, no extra words, no signature, no watermark, no mockup, no hands, no brush or ink bottle in the picture.

Landscape image, 1536x1024.

SUBJECT: a page of separate hand-painted marks that will be cut out and used as decoration on a web page. Generously spaced, nothing touching, nothing crossing the page edge:
- three horizontal underline strokes of different lengths (one fairly straight, one slightly wavy, one short and thick);
- two loose hand-drawn arrows (one curving to the right, one curving downwards);
- one quick oval loop, as if circling a word (open, with the ends overlapping);
- two hand-drawn rectangular frames in portrait proportion (about 4:5), with wobbly sides and corners that overshoot or don't quite meet, drawn with a thinner line than the rest;
- one short horizontal divider line with a tiny loop in the middle.

No text, no numbers, no letters.
